text: Hello, welcome to This is my architecture. My name is Daniel and I'm here with Juan
Cho from Equinix. Juan Cho, tell us a little bit about what Equinix does.
Equinix is the largest data center and color provider in the world and from Equinix professional
services we help our customers to design new architecture for the cloud.
Okay, so you brought us an architecture that you developed in your company, so what's this about?
This started as an ad tech architecture, then later we moved to introduce to other solutions that needed
large amounts of data in-guest. In this case was the interactions of the users in the internet,
so every time that you see an advertising or an ad in a site or you do a click, we are going to
receive your interaction through this architecture. Okay, so it sounds like you can analyze what's
going on when a user has an intent to buy something, so how exactly is the data flow? Yes, for example,
here we have the users, so imagine that you are the user, you are looking at your newspaper,
I mean not the paper, but your new site, so we are going to receive through CloudFront your interaction,
that you saw something. This interaction is going to pass through ECS that we are using because it's a
Docker cluster container system that is going to manage everything for us, so we don't need to worry
about anything there. Our receivers usually are writing in Go, we choose Go because it's more easy and
more faster to compile. And then this is going to send all of the events to this Kinesis Firehost
service. Kinesis Firehost is going to manage for us the stream in another way, so we can have all of
your interactions of the user interactions in one place. As the data is going to pass through this
Kinesis Firehost, Kinesis Firehost is going to save the raw data in S3. So we can have every interaction
that you had with the websites that we work. Then at some point, like every five minutes, we have a Lambda
here that is going to do an aggregation of all of the data that we have in S3. So for example, if a user
did a click in one app, we are going to check if you did have some interactions before. This is like a
traditional ad tech solutions, but in a new way, you know, in an Amazon Web Services way. So after we have the
aggregation data, we are going to write down again to S3 the output of this data so we can have some
dashboards for the business users where they can see all of the analytics related to the business,
you know, like interactions, conversions, etc. At the same time, this Lambda is going to write in
DynamoDB some outputs or aggregation that is important for these dashboards that the users
from the backend or from the business are going to consume. And these users are going to access
this data and this real-time analytics data through API Gateway. So we don't need to have
servers or anything there. It's totally serverless. These users are going to access the DynamoDB data
and the streaming data. For example, the real-time interactions, how many users are coming through
this platform at some point in an online or real-time way. This architecture right now is usually for
the largest customer that we have receiving like 15,000 events per second. That's a large amount of
data. And it allows our customers to have a solution that requires new ops because everything is managed by
Amazon Web Services. Everything is cost-tracked so we can have the price per event that's going to take,
I mean the price is going to be to process one event across all of the infrastructure because we know that
the price for Kinesis, we know the price for CloudFront, etc. And everything is going to be protected by Amazon Shield.
So right now for this scenario we are using Shield. So if the website that is hosting the advertising receives
an attack or something, this attack is going to generate more traffic, we can prevent this traffic
to go to the invoice of the customer because Shield is going to cover that. So normally if you wouldn't have
Shield, what would happen? So it would scale up or...? It's going to scale up, it's going to accept the traffic,
but the problem is the customer is going to need to pay for that transfer, data transfer and usage.
If you have Shield, Shield is going to protect your environment from the cost perspective because we are
also using CloudFront and WAV, the web application firewall to protect from attacks. But that's a different
perspective on security. Yeah, so it sounds you put a lot of effort into designing this for being secure and
also performant. Sounds like a great sample also of serverless and using managed services. So usually,
do you have any samples where this might be in terms of scalability, there might be some
boundaries that you reach or how does the system generally behave when it's at a high load?
Well, we reached some limits with ECS at the beginning because we needed to have more workers
and also because of the amount of data that we are pushing through the platform was some kind of
complicated when we started designing this solution to fine-tune the lambdas, you know, that you have some
time per lambda execution and also we are having a lot of traffic here. You know, Kinesis is 20 000
message per seconds because we have more message here than in the input. You know, in the input we have
the raw things, the interactions, one click, one conversion, one interaction. But here we have the
aggregation and we are doing also analytics on the data. And that generates more messages inside of the system.
Yeah, but everything is covered by Amazon Web Services. And I mean, this is a no-ops infrastructure.
Yeah, sounds great. So basically any customer that you propose this kind of architecture
knows that he doesn't have to run servers and is fully managed, right?
Yeah, and we are using this kind of solution for different customers. It's a problem solution
that we like to offer to our customers. And it can scale in different blocks. So you can scale in ECS if
you have more amount of data. You can scale with DynamoDB if you need to store more aggregation data. You
can fine-tune how much data you want to aggregate. So it's very scalable and very flexible for the customer.
Great. So Juanjo, thanks for showing us this kind of architecture. I think it's a good sample of managed services and serverless
for massive data and processing. And yeah, thanks for being on the show.
Thank you for inviting me and hope to be here next time.
So thanks for watching. This is my architecture.
